newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down, unfazed by budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down, unfazed by budget cuts.

text.p: Despite the Thai cabinet's decision to cut government spending by 99 billion baht in fiscal 1996/97, investors on Tuesday sold stocks amid tight liquidity, driving the index down slightly, brokers said.

"Investors have discounted news on Tuesday's cabinet approval to cut government spending as it's not a fresh news for them anymore. What worried them most today was about liquidity in the money market which was still tight today," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
The SET composite index, which moved in negative territory throughout the session, slipped 3.24 points to 733.99.
The SET-50 index dropped 0.23 point to 53.45. Decliners led advancers 166 to 142 while 96 issues unchanged.
The overnight interbank rate slipped to 12.00-12.50 percent late on Tuesday against 14.00-16.00 early today.
Brokers said although the overnight interbank rate had improved, it was still high and liquidity in the money market was still tight.
"I think foreigners were not active today as the market was still on a downward trend," Somchai said.
The banking sector dropped 0.14 percent while the communication sector retreated 0.98 percent and the property sector slipped 2.95 percent. The finance sector gained 1.15 percent.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 0.25 baht to 44.50. National Finance and Securities gained 0.50 to 39.50 while large capitalised Finance One increased 1.25 to 31.75 and Tipco Asphalt in the building and furnishing materials sector fell one to 148.
